OpenAI Lowers Funding Target and Valuation
The
ChatGPT
maker is now seeking about $20 billion in its latest funding round, down $10 billion from its original target, the Financial Times reported Friday, citing people familiar with the matter.
OpenAI has also lowered its desired valuation to $1.25 trillion from $1.4 trillion, the report said.

The company set a Friday deadline for investors to commit to the round. However, the report said the initial close is expected to bring in less than $20 billion after some investors reduced their allocations.
OpenAI did not immediately respond to Benzinga’s request for comment.
UAE Investors Expected to Lead OpenAI Funding Round
A consortium of UAE investors, including state-backed technology fund
MGX
, is expected to be the largest participant in the funding round.
As part of the arrangement, OpenAI could reportedly secure an option to lease newly developed computing capacity in the region.
Venture capital firms
Founders Fund
Coatue, Sequoia Capital
and
Andreessen Horowitz
are also expected to participate. Wealthy individuals could get another opportunity to invest through a subsequent retail offering at a $1.25 trillion valuation.
Last week, the publication also reported that OpenAI is looking to

This valuation would represent an increase of nearly 50% from its current $852 billion valuation, but falls short of the $1.4 trillion figure the company had earlier discussed with prospective investors.
AI Stock Selloff Raises Investor Concerns
The fundraising pullback comes as U.S. technology stocks face mounting pressure over massive AI infrastructure investments.
The tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite fell about 2.9% Friday and is down 7.8% from its Oct. 6 record closing high.
